pi_items.source: ESA Hubble FITS Liberator NGC 6652 dataset page confirms 555nm V-band filter data available as 555wmos.zip (6.5MB compressed). Setup script targets this file at line 40-46 searching for '555' in filename.

STScI WFPC2 Data Handbook Chapter 1 (https://www.stsci.edu/hst/wfpc2/Wfpc2_dhb/wfpc2_ch1.html) specifies 0.0996 arcsec/pixel for WFPC2 Wide Field chips (WF2, WF3, WF4). 0.1 arcsec/pixel is the standard rounded value used in practice and is what the setup script uses (line 22 of setup_task.sh).

pi_items.verified_value: WFPC2 Wide Field chips (WF2, WF3, WF4)
pi_items.source: ESA Hubble and NOIRLab confirm WFPC2 as the instrument. Setup_task.sh comments (line 22, 58) confirm Wide Field configuration with plate scale 0.1 arcsec/pixel.

pi_items.metadata_value: Ground truth computed from real data during setup
pi_items.verified_value: Setup script uses real image data: detects bright stars via Gaussian filtering and high threshold (99.5th percentile), identifies close pairs with 15-40 pixel separation and moderate flux ratio (1.2x to 5x), computes separation in arcseconds using plate scale, position angle using atan2(dx, dy), and magnitude difference using aperture flux ratio.
pi_items.source: setup_task.sh lines 76-189 implement star detection and pair selection algorithm; ground truth saved to /tmp/double_star_ground_truth.json with keys: plate_scale, primary_x, primary_y, primary_flux, secondary_x, secondary_y, secondary_flux, separation_pixels, separation_arcsec, position_angle_deg, magnitude_difference

privileged_info_summary: Task uses real NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope WFPC2 data of NGC 6652 globular cluster acquired through the F555W (V-band, 555nm) filter, downloaded from ESA Hubble FITS Liberator. WFPC2 Wide Field chips have a plate scale of 0.0996 arcsec/pixel (rounded to 0.1 in practice). Setup script detects bright stars in the real 2048x2048 pixel image, identifies a close pair with 15-40 pixel separation (1.5-4.0 arcsec), and computes ground truth measurements (separation, position angle, magnitude difference) from centroid positions and aperture photometry. Verifier compares agent measurements against these dynamically computed values.
